weakness: The put-down (handover) spot was a hard-coded table coordinate. With a fixed block standing there, the left arm drove the mug into the block and knocked it off; the right arm then had nothing graspable (10/10 failures). The program had no notion of free space, of other supporting surfaces, or of whether the second arm could reach the object where the first arm leaves it. Repair exposed three more weaknesses: grasps tried only the first reachable candidate even when its final approach was blocked, the pre-place pose 5 cm above a raised surface was out of reach, and a placement that 'succeeded' could leave the mug where the other arm cannot grasp it.
how_found: Questioned A1 (the hard-coded handover spot is empty): it is the only location in the program that is a constant instead of something perceived, and real tables are cluttered.
why_missed: In the nominal scene the spot is always free and the expert's coordinates suit both arms, so the choice of spot never had to be justified or checked.
fix: Put-down spot chosen at run time: candidates are free table cells (>= 8 cm from averaged obstacle footprints, roomy ones first) and flat tops of perceived boxes wide enough for the mug body. A candidate is used only if the receiving arm has a reachable grasp of the mug at that hypothetical pose and the placing arm's placement plans (pre-approach shortened to 2 cm for raised surfaces). The planner gets inflated obstacle boxes; grasps fall through all reachable candidates; the landing is verified (upright, within 4 cm). Recovered to 0.6 only: the block occupies exactly the zone both arms reach, so feasible spots sit at the edge of both workspaces and depend on which grasp the first arm happened to take.
general_rule: Never hard-code where an object is put down or handed over; choose the spot at run time from perceived free support surfaces (including tops of objects) and accept it only if both the placing motion and the next arm's grasp there are reachable.
unsolved_reason: Within 6 repairs the pipeline reached 0.6. Full recovery would need choosing the first arm's grasp with the handover in mind (or an in-air handover), because whether any spot is feasible depends on the grasp taken before the spot is chosen.

weakness: Arm roles were hard-coded: the left arm always fetched and the right arm always hung. With the rack on the far left the right arm could not reach the hook (0/10). Repair exposed three deeper faults in the hang itself. The carry to the hook was planned without the rack, so the mug in the hand swept into the rack's post and turned in the grip. The in-hand pose measured right after lifting was stale by the time the handle reached the hook (off by 3-12 cm and up to ~50 deg), so the single precomputed insertion missed and the mug fell. And a correction move that also held the gripper orientation was infeasible, because the corrected pose has a different orientation.
how_found: Three earlier designs (a 0.35 kg slippery mug, the rack turned 1 rad, the mug moved to the right half) were all rejected because the frozen pipeline still scored 0.8. The remaining hard-coded choice in the program was which arm does which job (A3), so I moved the goal fixture to the other side.
why_missed: In every nominal layout the rack stands on the right, so assigning arms by habit always worked. The hang was only ever executed by the arm whose carry path happens to stay clear of the rack, so the in-hand drift never mattered.
fix: Arm roles now come from the scene: the arm on the hook's side hangs, and the mug is handed over only if it starts on the other side. The mug is carried slowly to a staging pose 12 cm out along the hook axis, with the rack as an obstacle, then waits 0.5 s to settle. At the hook's mouth the measured handle is servoed onto the entrance (re-measure, correct, up to 3 times, ignoring implausible jumps over 8 cm). The handle then slides in slowly on a fixed gripper orientation, falling back to an unconstrained slide.
general_rule: Decide which arm does what from the perceived layout, not by habit, and before a precision insertion re-measure the held object at the target's entrance and correct until it is aligned, because objects shift and turn in the hand while they are carried.

weakness: The rack was measured once before the hang. Staging, servo and slide all aimed at that pose, so a rack pushed ~8 cm during the carry made every insertion miss (0/10). The round-2 servo loop corrected only the held mug, never the hook it aimed at. Repair exposed a second staleness: waiting for the target to come to rest while holding the mug made the in-hand pose measured before the wait wrong too (the mug settles in the hand during any pause). That put the staging pose out of reach and briefly dropped the base task to 0.7.
how_found: Questioned A6 for the target instead of the grasped object. The servo added in round 2 re-measures only what is in the hand. Two other designs failed to break the pipeline: clutter sliding into the handover spot was absorbed because the spot is chosen late.
why_missed: In every scene so far the rack was fixed, so perceiving the target once was always valid, and the round-2 repair treated the target pose as ground truth.
fix: Before the hang, wait until the rack is still: two 40-sample averages 1 s apart within 8 mm, for up to 10 s. Measure the in-hand mug only after that wait. In the servo loop, re-measure the hook every iteration and re-aim (waiting for stillness again) if it moved by more than 1 cm. Final eval: base 0.8, v5 0.9, v7 1.0.
general_rule: Right before a precision step, re-measure the target as well as the held object, wait until the target is still, and take every measurement the step uses after the last pause, because both the target and the object in hand can move while you wait.

weakness: Everything about the hang was tuned to RoboTwin's mugs 0-9. With the larger, unseen mug 12, the grasp chosen by preference left the hook unreachable on most seeds (the handle sits further from the grip), and the program just pushed on. Repairs uncovered three more faults. The fixed insertion stalled: the big loop met the hook's tip and was held back while the gripper slid along it, so the handle stopped 7-10 cm short. The program then released anyway, because a completed motion was taken as a completed insertion. And after a good hang, the retreat move failed, an immediate check of the still-swinging mug said 'not hung', and the arm's return home knocked it off the rack.
how_found: Questioned A9 (the mug is the size of the training mugs). RoboTwin ships three mug models the task never uses, and model 12 is the largest; a real robot meets mugs of every size.
why_missed: All training mugs are similar enough that the default grasp, the fixed 5 cm insertion and an open-loop release always worked, so neither grasp choice nor engagement was ever checked.
fix: Six repairs: (1) if a hang move is unreachable with the current grasp, put the mug back and regrasp with an untried contact point; (2) after release, withdraw along the approach axis as far as is reachable, then lift, and judge success only after the mug settles, never touching a hung mug again; (3) a stepwise slide with lateral gating (worse, reverted); (4) insertion depth computed from the rack's geometry, with a tighter servo; (5) release only if the handle is measured past the tip, otherwise keep holding, back out and regrasp; (6) when the insertion stalls, search +-1.5 cm offsets across the axis. v8 peaked at 0.3 (repairs 1 and 5) and ended at 0.2. The base task and the accepted v5 and v7 all reached 1.0 with these repairs. The expert, with ground truth, also fails v8 10/10, which suggests this model's handle keypoint does not describe an opening the hook can thread from this approach.
general_rule: Never take a finished motion as a finished insertion: before letting go, measure that the object is actually engaged at its goal, and if it is not, keep holding it, back out, and retry with a different alignment or grasp; after letting go, withdraw along a verified-free path and judge the result only once the object has settled.
unsolved_reason: The handle of this unseen mug stalls at the hook's tip whatever the grasp, depth or small offsets (the expert fails all seeds too); a fix would need perceiving the real handle opening rather than the annotated keypoint, which the API does not provide.

weakness: The program assumed the object can always be grasped where it lies. Every grasp it uses comes from above, followed by a straight lift. With a shelf 2 cm above the mug no grasp was plannable, and the program gave up at once (0/10): it had no way to change where the object is before grasping it. Repairs showed that the motions needed to slide the mug out sit at the edge of the arms' reach. Low horizontal gripper poses are mostly unreachable, the wrist cannot pass under an inflated obstacle box, the arm that looks natural for a direction is often the one that cannot get in, and a push that only just clears the overhang leaves the object where the next grasp collides with it or out at the table edge.
how_found: Questioned A7 (the space above the object is free): all the object's grasp points are approached from above and every grasp ends in a straight lift, so anything overhead removes every option at once.
why_missed: Nothing ever stood above an object in the nominal scenes, so the approach direction was never a choice and grasping 'where it lies' always worked.
fix: Detect overhangs: perceived boxes whose footprint covers the object and whose underside is above the table. Then slide the object out before grasping, with the closed gripper pointing forward and tilted 17 deg down (reachability probes showed horizontal poses at table height are mostly unreachable). Try every arm/direction pairing and three contact offsets toward the open edge, plan against the overhang's perceived box rather than an extra-inflated one, push 7 cm clear, prefer exits towards the table's middle, and verify the object is actually clear. Reached 0.2 (base, v5 and v7 stayed at 1.0).
general_rule: When an object cannot be grasped where it is, first move it to where it can be (for example slide it out with a push the arm can actually reach, trying each arm and direction), and confirm it is clear and reachable before planning the grasp.
unsolved_reason: The shelf covers the whole start region with 2 cm clearance; the pushes that clear it need the wrist at the limit of both arms' reach, so only some layouts admit a long enough push, and pushes sometimes tip the mug or leave it out of reach. A real fix needs other non-prehensile motions (a hooked finger pulling the mug) or a different grasp family.

weakness: After the hand-over, the program checked that the mug stood within 4 cm of where it was set down and gave up the whole task if not. A mug nudged ~10 cm right after release made every episode stop at that check (0/10), although the mug was still upright and perfectly graspable where it ended up.
how_found: Read the checks added in earlier rounds and asked what each does when it fails: the landing check was the only one whose failure branch aborted instead of re-planning.
why_missed: The check was written to catch a mug that fell over during placement. In every scene so far a mug that was not at the spot had also fallen over, so 'not where I put it' and 'unrecoverable' always coincided.
fix: After the hand-over, wait until the mug is still (two 40-sample averages 1 s apart), then continue from where it actually is if it is upright; whether it still sits on a raised support is decided from its measured height. Before every grasp of the hanging arm, also wait until the mug is still. Final eval: base 0.9, v5 1.0, v7 1.0, v13 1.0.
general_rule: When a check finds the world different from what the plan expected, treat it as new information: wait until things are still, re-perceive, and continue from the actual state, and abort only if the task has really become impossible.

weakness: Obstacles were measured once, at the start. A tall post that glided in after the first look, ending between the hand-over area and the rack, was invisible to every later plan: the mug in the hanging arm was swung into it, turned in the grip, and every pose computed from the garbled in-hand measurement was absurd (0/10). Repairs exposed further faults. The planner models only the arm, so carries planned around obstacles still drove the held mug into them. When the scene changed next to the mug, the hanging arm could no longer approach it, and the program had no way to move it again. The extra safety margin on obstacle boxes closed the real gap beside the mug. A failed put-back left the mug dangling while the other arm reached for it.
how_found: Questioned A13: the obstacle list is computed once at the start, and in round 6 only the mug was allowed to move. People and objects entering the workspace mid-task are the commonest change a real robot sees.
why_missed: In every scene so far, everything that was in the way was already there at the first look, so one obstacle snapshot per episode was enough.
fix: Six repairs: (1) re-perceive the obstacles (waiting until they are still) before each phase and plan with the fresh boxes; (2) while carrying, plan against obstacles grown by how far the held mug sticks out, lifting straight up before turning; (3) if the hanging arm can no longer take the mug, have the other arm move it to a spot chosen from the current scene; (4) plan grasps against the obstacles as perceived, without the extra margin; (5) reliable put-back and release before a regrasp or redo; (6) stage closer to the hook when the usual staging pose is blocked. v16 stayed at 0.0-0.1. The base task and the accepted v5, v7 and v13 stayed at 0.9-1.0 throughout.
general_rule: Re-perceive obstacles before every phase rather than once per task, plan carrying motions against obstacles enlarged by the held object's extent, and when a change in the scene blocks the next step, redo the previous step from the current scene instead of giving up.
unsolved_reason: The post ends next to the line along which the hanging arm must approach the hook (the hook's axis is fixed by the rack), so for these rack positions every staging pose the hanging arm can reach with the grasps it can take collides with the post. The post is fixed, so the scene probably admits no hang for most seeds; the expert oracle also failed 10/10.

weakness:
The program had no way to make room. With tall movable objects standing a finger's width from the mug on all four sides, every grasp approach was refused and the program gave up (0/10). Repairs exposed the parts of 'making room' it lacked:
- Crowding objects have no grasp keypoints, so they need a manual grasp from straight above.
- A pinch can miss, and the object must be re-detected before retrying.
- The nearest free spot is usually in the working corridor, so a moved object becomes the next obstacle.
- Far-out spots are often out of reach.
- Planning from among crowding objects fails outright, because the arm already sits inside their safety margins.
- An object released above the table falls over and becomes a new obstacle.
how_found: Questioned A12 (only the task objects are near the mug): real counters are crowded, and every grasp the program knows needs free space around the object.
why_missed: The nominal table holds only the mug and the rack, so some grasp approach was always free and 'make room first' never came up.
fix:
Six repairs:
(1) When no grasp works, find movable objects crowding the mug, move them one at a time with a straight-down grasp, re-perceive, and retry.
(2) Re-detect and turn the fingers 90 deg after a missed pinch; send objects far out on the arm's own side.
(3) Choose destinations about 0.36 m out, within reach.
(4) Return home before clearing, and lift clear of the crowd after the grasp.
(5) If every plan fails with the safety margins, retry against the boxes as perceived.
(6) Always set a moved object down before releasing it, and lift the held mug to a safe height.
v17 reached 0.2-0.3. The base task and the accepted v5, v7 and v13 ended at 1.0.
general_rule: When the target is boxed in, make room first: move the neighbours one at a time to reachable spots outside the working corridor, set each one down before letting go, and plan every next motion from a free start (lift clear of the crowd), re-perceiving after each move.
unsolved_reason: Only some neighbours and destinations are reachable for the arm on the mug's side. After the mug is grasped among the remaining neighbours, the hand-over placements stay unplannable on most seeds, so 2-3 of 10 seeds complete within 6 repairs.

weakness: The hand-over assumed that some table spot is reachable by both arms. A fixed divider between the arms' halves left no such spot except awkwardly around the divider's front end. The program then tried spot after spot, each pre-place move succeeding and each final descent being refused, and gave up when its list ran out (8/10 failed). The in-air hand-over added in repair exposed a reach problem: the fetching arm holds the mug with its wrist ~23 cm above it, so lifting the mug over a 30 cm divider asks for gripper poses near 1.33 m, out of reach. Asking the placement helper for the mug's current orientation also re-aligned the mug and swung the gripper 20 cm sideways.
how_found: Questioned A7 for the hand-over: after the hand-over spot became a run-time choice (round 1), the program still assumed open table connects the two arms' halves.
why_missed: The table was always open between the arms, so the spot search always found a common spot and no other hand-over mode was ever needed.
fix: Four repairs: (1) an in-air hand-over when no table spot works for both arms (hold the mug above the obstacle, the other arm grasps it, the first lets go); (2) carry the held mug by pure translation of the gripper; (3) hold it just above the obstacle's true top, lowest first; (4) extend the spot search toward the divider's end and try more spots. v20 stayed at 0.2. The run's time budget ended here, so the variation was stopped after 4 of the 6 allowed repairs. Base and the accepted variations stayed at 0.8-1.0.
general_rule: Before committing to a hand-over, check that a hand-over pose exists that both arms can actually reach (a shared surface, around an obstacle's end, or in the air at a reachable height), and choose the fetching arm's grasp so its wrist does not put that pose out of reach.
novel_note: Refines round 1's rule (choose the hand-over at run time and accept it only if both arms reach it) with the in-air and around-the-end options.
unsolved_reason: With the wrist ~23 cm above the held mug, any pose that lifts the mug over the 30 cm divider is out of reach, and table spots around the divider's end are reachable for the placing arm on only a few seeds. Stopped after 4 repairs by the run's time budget.
